methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.

original_card.acceptance_gate: Require a legal chronological rewrite and favorable complete signed target-minus-paid moment with all extra charges. Unchanged ADD counts or unchanged paid-call counts alone decide neither success nor failure. Compiler, native and outer admission remain separate obligations.

original_card.first_experiment: Construct one legal source-bound rewrite and compare complete before/after P and T. Charge restoration, source windows and owned helpers. A paid call need not disappear: a legal target split or rank redistribution may win. Stop if the signed moment is unchanged or the consumer repays the gain. Do not extend a scalar-only census on ADD counts.

actual_scope: Prove that the complete signed raw moment of the merged binary query-tree bill (research/balanced-query-tree, PR6348) has exactly one zero on all of t>0, by Laguerre's tail-sum rule of signs, with an exact reusable checker.
scope_change_reason: No rewrite is constructed. The card's acceptance gate is a favourable complete signed moment; this package settles the sign of that moment for one existing bill at every exponent, which the source check settles only below the 0.0034 BIT cap. The rule is a reusable certificate where the Descartes budget used by the power-variation tools is too weak.
bottleneck_link: Side result on pricing: every κ claim compares complete target and paid power sums. A global sign certificate rules out a second favourable window and needs no interval engine.
stop_rule: Stop after one exact certificate on one merged bill; do not survey other bills.
evidence: research/tail-sum-crossing-uniqueness/verify.py prints PASS_TAIL_SUM_CROSSING_UNIQUENESS; PROOF.md gives the argument.

open_questions.question: How many merged complete bills have exactly one tail-sum sign change, and does adding this rule to the power-variation tools settle invoices they report as inconclusive?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Descartes budget counts roots at t<=0 as well; the tail-sum count only sees t>0, so it can be much smaller (13 versus 1 here).
open_questions.first_step: Run certify() on the invoices that scripts/compare_power_variation.py reports as inconclusive.
open_questions.blocked_by: None; this package does not modify the shared script.

open_questions.question: Can a tail-sum count on (0,1) alone be obtained, for example by combining tail sums of c_r and of c_r r?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Roots at t>1 (negative savings) are irrelevant, yet still consume this budget.
open_questions.first_step: Tail sums of c_r r bound roots on t>1; find a valid way to combine the two counts or prove none exists.
open_questions.blocked_by: Subtracting two upper bounds does not give an upper bound.
